title: One ad owns all the lag
description: Click events are partitioned by ad ID. One viral ad pins a processor while others idle. You need to spread its events without sending retries of one click to unrelated dedupe states. Which plan preserves the counting boundary?

options.text: Choose a fresh random salt for every produce attempt and merge partial counts later.
options.explanation: A retry can receive a different salt and evade shard-local dedupe, inflating counts when partials are summed.

options.text: Add consumer tasks but leave the hot ad on its existing single partition.
options.explanation: Extra consumers cannot concurrently split ownership of that same partition's keyed state.

options.text: Drop events for the hot ad once its processor falls behind.
options.explanation: Billing counts require a recovery and reconciliation path, not unrecorded load shedding.

options.text: Salt by a stable hash of click ID, deduplicate and count per sub-key, then merge partial counts per ad and window.
options.explanation: Retries of one click reach the same sub-key, while distinct clicks spread across processors. The merge sees a small set of partials instead of every click; version the scheme if its salt count changes.
